question: What is website accessibility and why does it matter?
answer: Website accessibility means your site can be used by everyone, including visitors using screen readers, keyboard-only navigation, or who have visual impairments — covering things like alt text on images, sufficient colour contrast, labelled form fields, and a logical heading structure. Beyond serving roughly 1 in 5 visitors with some form of disability, accessible sites tend to have cleaner underlying code that also helps SEO, and accessibility is increasingly a legal requirement in many sectors.
